channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Nearly half of vapers would consider black-market products as October tax approaches, new survey finds
item.description: Nearly half of vapers considering black-market products should be read as a warning about policy design. A tax that makes legal vaping less affordable can push people towards unregulated supply, where product standards, age checks and consumer protection are weaker. That does not strengthen public health; it shifts risk into places authorities struggle to control. Taxation should discourage smoking without making safer legal alternatives less attractive than the black market. (Published on September 09, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: When Nicotine Is Treated as Synonymous with Smoking, Science—and People—Lose
item.description: Equating nicotine with smoking is one of the most damaging shortcuts in public health communication. Nicotine can cause dependence, but the major burden of disease comes from inhaling smoke from combustible tobacco. Blurring that distinction leaves smokers confused about safer alternatives and less able to judge their options realistically. Clearer policy should target the harms of combustion while giving adults honest information about lower-risk nicotine products. (Published on September 09, 2026bysubstack.com)
